details.summary: Preserve two reusable lessons: repair PDF quotations from stored source text, and distinguish missing biographical evidence from extraction omissions. Retain the existing discovery memory.

edits.title: Repair PDF quotations using exact source slices
edits.content: PDF extraction can interleave columns and whitespace, making a plausible reconstructed quotation noncontiguous. When quote membership fails, locate the relevant passage in the stored fetched text and copy an exact contiguous slice, preserving intervening text and whitespace. Verify that the slice supports the complete value and belongs to the correct person. If the layout prevents clear support, fetch an alternative source. Recheck membership before replacing the failed cell; detecting a mismatch alone is not a completed repair.

edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

additional_candidates.description: Exact membership validation detected a noncontiguous affiliation quotation in extracted PDF text.
Focused source reviews distinguished absent nationality evidence from birthplace and separated employment affiliations from education.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, but the visible trajectory ends during ongoing research after searches for unresolved nationality fields. It shows neither a final submission attempt nor a terminal failure explaining the absence. A new completion rule would duplicate the existing output contract without an established cause.

All 32 occurrences were considered. Signals 0–6 correspond to seven annual searches whose inspected snippets lacked laureate names; their empty discoveries were honest. Signals 7–31 correspond to 25 nationality searches for people already identified in extracted rows, so they could advance field research without discovering new entities. The existing memory explicitly permits honest empty discoveries for verification searches and was followed here. Its usage and outcomes arrays contain no consistently bad outcomes warranting revision or deletion.

The extraction diagnostic reports one failed affiliation quote, and the subsequent inspection prints the malformed quotation. No completed repair is visible. This supports a failure memory about exact source slicing and revalidation, beyond the base instruction to check membership. The existing discovery memory addresses a different failure mode and should remain unchanged.

Extraction left nationality unresolved rather than inferring it. Focused reviews confirmed source absence across the affected releases and distinguished secondary appointments from Ph.D. institutions; subsequent targeted searches found explicit nationality and citizenship leads. This supports the diagnostic procedure as a skill, while not claiming that those leads were fetched or the final table completed. No existing entry covers this procedure.
